question: Does retained Fr 20274 text distinguish one previously published Compassio Mariae antiphon version?
scope: Identification of the selected surviving Magnificat-antiphon ending only, not the entire office or a codex
new_source_observation: Above its matins invitatory, Fr 20274 preserves the differentiating nobis vite spem porrexit / presidens in gloria / Fac nos Virgo ending of O Maria stans sub cruce. It does not reproduce the different tam prolixus / ille dulcis crucifixus ending visible on the retained older C23 71v page.

secondary_word_candidates.cum_dum: Target provisionally cum; the edition's C435 base text prints dum while its apparatus reports cum for C23, C21 and several other witnesses.
secondary_word_candidates.feruere_perfrui: Target provisionally feruere; the apparatus reports this for C23, C21 and multiple other witnesses, versus perfrui in the edited base text.
secondary_word_candidates.limit: Shared readings across several witnesses cannot identify one book, one exemplar or a unique transmission branch. C435 manuscript readings remain editorial reports pending originals.

Urberg2016.locator: Printed pp.247-267, especially pp.254-257; PDF273-293, especially PDF280-283; full relevant range read, figures checked.
Urberg2016.statement: The dissertation already analyses C23's textual and musical redactions and the replacement of its longer antiphons. Its historical reconstruction is prior scholarship, not this project's discovery.
Urberg2016.read_status: Relevant range read; the full 996-page PDF was text-searched, not read in its entirety.

Hallqvist2020.locator: Printed p.4 / PDF51 (shorter ending and apparatus); p.19 / PDF66 (older ending); introduction p.x / PDF15 (C435 photo access). Relevant complete pages visually checked.
Hallqvist2020.statement: The edition already prints the two versions and the cum/dum and feruere/perfrui witness distributions. Its edited text is kept separate from actual source readings.

limits: Exploratory literature-assisted AI reading, not independent confirmation.
The candidate incipit is inferred from the differentiating ending; the incipit itself is not retained.
One passage cannot assign the whole office to a single recension; mixed textual states remain possible.
A shared standard version is not a unique lineage, date, production-site or physical same-codex fingerprint.
Urberg's account concerns historical changes to C23; it does not date this target or establish dependence on C23.
The specific C23 added/replacement page 69r and C435 original pages are not locally inspected.
Full-text searches found none of the four target numbers checked, but this does not clear novelty or exclude other scholarship, identifiers or unindexed evidence.
No claim meets the project's original discovery standard, and none of the seven frozen ambiguous attribution cases is resolved.
access_dependency: Current C435 catalogue search met an Anubis verification page and was stopped. Hallqvist's statement about author-held photographs is dated 2020, not a claim about universal present access.
next_test: Inspect an explicitly identified, lawfully available C23 replacement page 69r and compare the retained target ending's original notation directly; re-read manuscript clefs and pitches before any melody claim. C435 originals could verify the reported lexical differences. Continue other unresolved attribution candidates independently.
